Transform standardized posterior samples back to original scale

Source: R/JAGS-formula-scale-transform.R
transform_scale_samples.Rd

Transforms posterior samples from standardized continuous predictors back to the original scale. This function is used when predictors were standardized during model fitting via the formula_scale parameter.

transform_scale_samples(fit, formula_scale = NULL)

Arguments

fit

a model fitted with JAGS_fit(). Matrices of posterior samples and other fit objects are not supported.

formula_scale

optional nested list containing standardization information keyed by parameter name, replacing the formula_scale attribute of fit. Each parameter entry contains scaling info (mean and sd) for each standardized predictor, e.g., list(mu = list(mu_x1 = list(mean = 0, sd = 1))). An entry must name every predictor that fit standardized for that parameter. The transformation is derived from the fitted structure stored in fit: the fixed-effect design, a log intercept, and the random-effect SD structure.

Value

A numeric matrix of posterior samples transformed back to the original predictor scale, with chains merged in their existing order. When no scaling information is supplied, the function returns the sample matrix without changing its values, rather than returning the fitted object.

Details

The function transforms regression coefficients and intercepts to account for predictor standardization, including interactions of any order.

Columns that are not coefficients of the fitted design or random-effect SDs and correlations of a scaled block, such as the totals and allocation nodes of ordered priors, keep their fitted-scale values.

Internal standardized random-effect coordinates (latent xRE_Zx columns and realized xRE_COEFx columns) are omitted from the returned matrix. They do not have the same transformation as fixed coefficients or random-effect covariance summaries and must not be presented as original-scale coefficients. This omission also applies when no scaling information is supplied.

For a k-way interaction between standardized predictors, the expansion of \(\prod_{i} (x_i - \mu_i)/\sigma_i\) contributes to all lower-order terms. The contribution to a target term T from a source term S (where T is a subset of S's scaled components) is: $$(-1)^{|extra|} \cdot \prod_{i \in extra} \mu_i / \prod_{i \in S_{scaled}} \sigma_i$$ where \(extra = S_{scaled} \setminus T_{scaled}\). Terms with a multiply_by multiplier (see JAGS_formula()) additionally carry the ratio of the source to the target multiplier, \(m_S / m_T\). The posterior must contain every lower-order coefficient with a nonzero contribution from this expansion. If it does not, the function stops rather than returning an incomplete transformation.

For a fitted object, or formula-scale metadata created by JAGS_formula() or JAGS_fit(), the fixed-coefficient transformation is derived from the stored fixed-effect design (persisted factor levels and contrasts) and verified to reproduce the fitted linear predictor exactly, which also covers nested terms such as ~ f/x. Formulas whose centered terms induce lower-order effects that the fitted formula does not contain (e.g., ~ x + x:f with x standardized) have no original-scale representation, and the function stops.

The original-scale random-effect SDs and correlations of a block with a standardized slope are transformed the same way, from the fitted design of the block: when the standardized block columns equal the original-scale columns times a matrix \(A\), the block coefficients transform as \(A u\) and their covariance as \(A \Sigma A'\). A block whose original-scale design is not spanned by its own columns (a term that would have to be induced, such as the implied intercept of (0 + x | g)) has no such matrix. It keeps the pairing of coefficient names only when each retained contribution has identical fitted categorical coding and every omitted contribution is unrepresentable by the block's lower-order columns. Otherwise original-scale output is unavailable, with reason "original_scale_not_representable"; use fitted-scale output or include the needed lower-order terms in the block. A block that the fitted design does not hold (hand-built random-effect SD metadata) is transformed by the same pairing of names.

Conditions

Invalid arguments, including a formula_scale entry for a formula parameter the model does not have (also for a model without formula parameters) or a standardized predictor that is missing from the posterior, stop with an ordinary error. A condition of class BayesTools_formula_transform_unavailable (parents error and condition; the reason field names the cause, for example "incomplete_formula_scale" (a formula_scale entry that omits a predictor standardized in the fitted model; the fields parameter and predictors name them), "missing_fitted_design", "original_scale_not_representable", "original_scale_not_identified", "homogeneous_scaled_block" (hand-built metadata of a homogeneous-SD block with a scaled slope, which JAGS_formula() refuses), or "nonfinite_transform") reports a transformation that is structurally or numerically unavailable. A condition of class BayesTools_refit_required reports a fit whose stored formula declarations are missing or disagree.
